compiled_state.description:
## Observation

On the production MCP host, 2026-11-01 21:03-21:35 PST, one compaction sweep (`op=compact-sweep`) held the store write lock for 100-165 s per ticket while folding 10 tickets (journald evidence on `radiant-benighted-warbler` and `overweak-deviant-shelduck`). The build included `f3cb9223d8c` (bug `graspable-fabled-skylark`), which moved the authorship history walks out of the lock.

A canonical write waits at most about 181 s (30 s x 2 attempts x 3 passes). A writer that arrives just after a fold takes the lock gets it only when that one fold ends. The between-ticket hand-over fix in `radiant-benighted-warbler` does not shorten a single fold, so a fold that holds the lock for longer than a writer's budget still fails that write.

## Unknown

What a 100-165 s fold spends its time on under the lock has not been measured. `graspable-fabled-skylark` removed the unbounded `git log` walks; the remaining locked work (fold, ledger build, SNAPSHOT write, retire, commit) on a 300k-commit clone has not been profiled.

## Next check

Profile one locked fold on a copy of a large tickets clone (not the live store), timing each phase inside `_compact_locked` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py`), to find which phase dominates before choosing between moving it out of the lock and bounding the hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The phase that dominates a long locked fold is identified with timings from a large clone copy, recorded in a ticket comment.
- [ ] A fold on that clone copy holds the store write lock for less than a canonical writer's single-pass budget (60 s), or the remaining hold is justified in a comment with the measurement.
compiled_state.title: A single compaction fold holds the store write lock for 100-165 s, past a writer's single pass
